questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was just sent a link from a friend, and we ended up living in an Erasmus building close to the centre. I was through
https://prague-shared-flats.eu/
. Prague 7 (Hipser) and Prague 2 (Fashionable) are the best places to stay I would say.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of scammers, I met several people who were scammed by their landlords. The dormatories are all way out of the city centre.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration opens a week before the semester starts and ends two weeks after. Then you can enrolle in technically every subject and then taste a bit of everything before making your final choice. You will maybe experience being put in line for the popular courses, but most of the time you will eventually be enrolled, and otherwise the student administration will help you enroll in your pre-approved courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student administration are very helpful, and despite the overall bureaucratic system, they can make anything possible. Shoutout for them ladies!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: With help from the student administration, I was enrolled in all of the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax, you will get into the courses you need.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: highly dependent on the course you are taking. A rule of thumb is that the more Erasmus students at a course the easier it is to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Fewer students per class (nice!) and more 'highschool'-like teaching with presentations and assignments during the semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The European Economic Integration course was a helpful introduction to macroeconomics, and the teacher was Amarican so he was easy to understand.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome arrangement, but I mostly socilised outside the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find any other Erasmus student who can add you to a hiking/tennis/bouldering/whatever whatsappchat, and you have a great foundation for making friends and have a hobby.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dresden and Budapest were nice cities. Bohemian Switzerland for a great nature experince.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Prague is an international city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take the language course, join different whatsapp or fb groups to hang out with other erasmus people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The humor and the nightlife

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Take the language course, both for social and cultural reasons. 
2) Go to Bike Jesus or Ancarli for a good party
3) DSB or Czeske Drahy offer cheap train tickets (you can choose seats with table at the CD website)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and the opportunity to feel rich for half a year.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing out the first normal semester since Covid.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.answer: Yes
